Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

drop me a line phrase

also write to me, write me a few lines, send me a note, drop someone a line

classical

Cic. Att. 12.38.2: sīc scrībēs aliquid sī vacābis
Traupman p. 102: scrībe aliquid litterārum quandō vacās

Scrībe aliquid!

imperative of scrībō with aliquid

write something, drop me a line

Cicero to Atticus: the future scrībēs works as a friendly imperative.

Examples

  • tū, quoniam necesse nihil est, sīc scrībēs aliquid sī vacābis

    since there’s no need, just drop me a line if you have timeCic. Att. 12.38.2

  • Scrībe aliquid litterārum, quandō vacās.

    Drop me a line when you have time.Traupman p. 102

See also write, available.
